record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code and result files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal outcomes for an abliterated released model, testing the practical weight-edit version of the claim. It does not test the original difference-in-means direction intervention.
record.gate_note: The README directly reports original-versus-abliterated Qwen refusal counts for political and historical questions about 1989. It says no harmful-content prompts were used; its statement about harmful requests refers to model cards, so it is not included as a result. The activation-steering results concern political stance, not refusal, and do not test the claimed refusal direction.
record.test_reason: The study compares a released abliterated Qwen checkpoint with its original on the same engine and settings. It counts refusals on 1989 Tiananmen questions in three scripts. This bears on V2 (weight-edit abliteration removes refusal in released models) in a new setting: political-censorship refusals rather than harmful requests. The study does not compute or ablate a direction itself, so V1 and the other versions are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that abliteration removes refusal (in Qwen on 1989 questions) but does not remove PRC-aligned political bias. Script of the question matters more than abliteration, and in Bolt abliteration mainly increases acquiescence.
record.recipe_differences: This is a benchmark/study repository, not a replication of the original direction-ablation method. It compares released original and abliterated model checkpoints; the README does not specify the weight-edit recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Abliteration shifts political stance without removing PRC-aligned bias. In Qwen, Index S moves toward the ROC side (+0.25 to +0.38) but stays negative in Simplified Chinese. In Bolt, the shift is general acquiescence: P(yes) rises on both sides of each statement pair.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-direction abliteration has side effects on non-refusal behaviour (acquiescence, stance) and does not remove learned stances.

fits_no_version.finding: After abliteration, Qwen answered fewer Traditional-Chinese prompts in Simplified Chinese (42/81 to 12/81). It also stopped denying the ROC exists in Traditional answers (5 to 0 of 12) but only partly in Simplified (7 to 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abliteration alters output behaviours beyond refusal.

record.problems: The refusal result is limited to one model and a political/historical prompt set, not harmful requests. No uncertainty is stated for the refusal counts, and the README says the study did not use harmful-content prompts. The README identifies the paper as a work in progress and draft.
record.rows_left_out: No other README results directly measure refusal or the claimed refusal direction. The harmful-request statement refers to model cards rather than results from this repository; the steering results measure political stance, so neither is recorded as a row for these versions.

untested.parts: Refusal of harmful requests; the Nemotron Bolt pair (no refusal counts reported for it); any models beyond one Qwen quantised checkpoint; capability retention.
Not tested: no difference-in-means direction is computed, ablated or added.
Not tested. The three scripts concern political answers, not transfer of a refusal direction.

missing.what: No refusal counts are reported for the Bolt original-versus-abliterated pair, although refusals are a listed measure. Raw outputs in results/ could supply them.
Weight audit of the released abliterations: Qwen had 144 tensors changed across all 48 layers; Bolt had 100 tensors changed in blocks 15–75. This documents what the weight edit touched.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T2 to T3: the study tests released abliterated models on a new prompt domain (political censorship) rather than replicating the method. The README says no harmful-content prompts were used. The abliteration recipe of the community builds is unstated, so whether they use a difference-in-means direction is assumed. The activation-steering experiments (script and stance vectors) concern political stance, not refusal. This is a work-in-progress draft; only the README was read.

versions.untested_parts: Does not find or ablate the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, add that refusal direction, or test general capabilities after its removal.
Tests refusal on 1989 political/historical questions in one Qwen model, not refusals to harmful requests or other models.
Does not test jailbreak suppression of the refusal direction or training against its ablation.
Does not compare a single direction with an affine, cone, or multi-direction account of refusal.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions.
Tests scripts/languages for political-question answers, not transfer of the refusal direction across languages or model variants.
Does not vary how or when refusal is trained to test whether a removable direction forms.
Does not test reasoning models or refusal directions in them.
